method.deja_query: E135 Tomb Raider BVB separate UID Activity Termux background moderate CPUs 0-3 top-app foreground scheduling A/B floating Termux window performance
method.runcommand_probe: A harmless 20-second child proved parent Termux Activity process 11485, CPUs 0-7, and both cpuset and cpu controllers at /top-app before the game launch.
method.property_guard: allow-external-apps was enabled only until the exact RunCommand controller existed in /top-app, then termux.properties was restored byte-for-byte to SHA-256 89094537f49531dc9b380a0dec3a441b2fb92577e0a4f1db505790eb8b7025b0.
method.foreground_lifetime: The shared-UID Termux:X11 Activity remained a small visible freeform window above the fullscreen BVB Activity, keeping the Activity-owned controller, game, and bridge service in /top-app.

diagnostic_activation_pass.classification: activation proof excluded from the clean primary result

visual_evidence.interpretation: The inspected screenshot shows a real Lara frame behind the intentionally small Termux:X11 foreground window. It proves the BVB consumer continues rendering during foreground promotion; it belongs to the excluded diagnostic pass, not the clean timed pass.

diagnosis: Android scheduling was not a minor fourth-order issue after E134; it multiplied both translated game throughput and Bionic bridge throughput. Foreground placement reduced final-window socket waiting from 126.1 to 69.0 ms per present, descriptor-ring waiting from 116.6 to 12.2 ms, and descriptor-worker mean time from 74.3 to 19.9 microseconds. Average FPS rose from 2.2 to 7.0 without changing the bridge binary.
recommendation: Make the Activity-owned RunCommand launch and foreground lifetime a hardened default for BVB games. Reduce the visible X11 foreground surface without losing top-app placement. The next measured bridge bottleneck is semaphore wait plus shared stream/Submit2 at 59.4 ms per present; descriptor-ring waiting is now 12.2 ms and WSI is 1.54 ms.
claim_boundary: The clean 7.0-FPS result and the excluded 7.1-FPS activation pass agree, proving a target-specific scheduling gain. The clean run is one pass rather than an alternating cooled series, and the small foreground window is a temporary usability compromise, not the final architecture.
reuse: The exact E135 deja query returned no indexed implementation. The launch reused the repository's guarded RunCommandService property restoration, top-app validation, CPU-topology/affinity guard, paired-ADB Activity handoff, Wait-only ANR handling, and protected Steam/X identity checks.
